size.note: Females average larger than males. Figures are approximate.

summary: A large eagle of rivers and lakes. Adults have a white head, chest and tail, a chestnut body, and dark flight feathers. The call is a loud ringing yelp, often given by a pair together.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^7=128 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 64–256.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.
